papers.title: On the formal definition of average function for interval data
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the formal definition of average functions for interval data, extending classical aggregation theory beyond precise numerical values to the more general setting of real-valued intervals. Recognizing that interval data nat- urally arise in contexts involving imprecision or uncertainty, we examine how established notions of averages and aggregation functions can be generalized when the underlying domain is no longer restricted to the unit interval, but instead encompasses the entire real line. We analyze the impact of different admissible orders on intervals, particularly focusing on the lattice order and several total orders, and provide rigorous definitions of idempotency and mono- tonicity in this context. Furthermore, we adapt and study classical families of aggregation operators such as power means, minimum, maximum, and median to the interval setting, characterizing when these operators satisfy the properties required of average functions for intervals. Our results highlight that the choice of order plays a crucial role in the behavior and suitability of these operators. This work lays a foundation for the systematic aggregation of interval-valued information, with potential applications in statistics, decision making, and fields where data imprecision is inherent.

papers.title: Smooth maps onto regions in Euclidean spaces respecting height functions
papers.abstract: One of interest of the author lies in the canonical projections of the unit spheres and generalizations. He is interested in the canonical projections of embedded manifolds in the higher dimensional Euclidean spaces, including height functions, especially, their construction and representations by explicit equations. This is a kind of fundamental studies on construction or global theory on singularity theory of differentiable maps, closely related to differential geometry, differential topology, and algebraic geometry. Rather than knowing existence, construction has been difficult in certain senses. We construct smooth maps onto regions in Euclidean spaces locally modeled by height functions and show new examples. This is related to a pioneering study of the author, certain generalizations of the canonical projections of the unit spheres (, so-called special generic maps), and construction of them as projections of connected components of the zero sets of some smooth maps to some Euclidean spaces.

papers.title: Higher-order tangent and secant numbers, special-value integrals, and a common zero attractor
papers.abstract: We study two families of coefficients associated with powers of the tangent function and with products of the secant and tangent functions, and develop a unified treatment of the corresponding higher-order tangent and secant numbers. The first part establishes a common identity for even derivatives of $\tanh x$ and odd derivatives of $\operatorname{sech}x$. Combined with integral formulae for these derivatives, this yields finite power-integral representations for the normalized values $\zeta(2n+1)$ and $\beta(2n)$ and naturally introduces two polynomial families $P_n$ and $Q_n$. We determine several arithmetic and structural properties of these polynomials. In particular, we identify the exact content of $P_n$, prove that $Q_n$ is primitive, establish strict log-concavity and unimodality of their coefficient sequences, and describe their real zeros. For even indices each family has a unique negative real zero, and the two sequences of real zeros have the same limit. We also derive differential recurrences and generating functions for $P_n$ and $Q_n$. The generating functions lead to a global complex-singularity analysis. We construct a compact Jordan curve $\Gamma$ and prove that the complex zero sets of both $P_n$ and $Q_n$ converge to $\Gamma$ in Hausdorff distance. The normalized zero-counting measures converge weakly to the same equilibrium measure on $\Gamma$. We determine the logarithmic capacity of the enclosed compact set, give an explicit arclength density for the limiting measure, and compute its first moments. Numerical plots for $P_{20}$, $P_{50}$, $P_{100}$ and $P_{150}$ illustrate the zero-attractor theorem.

papers.title: Formalization of Langlands's Second Main Lemma for Local Epsilon Factors
papers.abstract: We describe the Lean 4 formalization of Langlands's Second Main Lemma for local epsilon factors over nonarchimedean local fields, in mixed and equal characteristic. The lemma compares the induction expressions attached to compatible characters of the intermediate fields of a bicyclic extension of prime-square degree. We explain the mathematical constructions and comparisons that constitute the proof, and identify their Lean declarations.
